title: Elastic commit bandwidth mapping & contingency
summary: Working spreadsheet to map committed GPU/throughput bands to headcount phasing and price sensitivity. Focus is on minimizing margin volatility from short-term token pricing swings while preserving burst capacity for PLG growth.
scenarios: Conservative: 40% reserved commit, low burst (keep 30% headroom), hiring slowed to 60% of requested - target runway preserved.
Baseline: 60% reserved commit, moderate burst (50% headroom), hires follow product backlog needs - moderate margin compression tolerated.
Aggressive: 80% reserved commit for better unit economics, large upfront hiring to support throughput, risk of lock-in if demand falls.
assumptions: Token-unit cost baseline = $0.0009 per tkn (hosted API mix) - sensitivity +/- 30%
Reserved GPU monthly cost baseline = $14k per pod (averaged across 8xA100 profiled runs)
Average tokens per request = 620 (mix: chat + embeddings + rerank)
Server utilization target (reserved) = 72% for stable latency SLO
Hiring ramp: ramp hire -> full productivity in 14 weeks, blended comp fully loaded = $250k/year
headcount_phasing: Q2-2026: +6 engineers (serving/runtime) -> incremental fully-loaded cost run-rate = $125k/mo
Q3-2026: +4 SRE/infra -> incremental cost = $83k/mo; bring reserved capacity to +2 pods
Q4-2026: +3 infra/tools (opt) -> incremental cost = $62k/mo; enable auto-quantization pilot
Q1-2027: hold hiring (review commit utilization) unless sustained monthly throughput growth > 12%
capacity_and_commit_model: Band A (Conserve): 40% commit -> reserved pods = 8 -> cover ~58% monthly token demand -> monthly reserved cost $112k
Band B (Balance): 60% commit -> reserved pods = 12 -> cover ~78% monthly token demand -> monthly reserved cost $168k
Band C (Optimize): 80% commit -> reserved pods = 16 -> cover ~93% monthly token demand -> monthly reserved cost $224k
Burst plan: maintain on-demand pool for seasonal spikes up to 25% of peak; conversion trigger = 6 consecutive weeks of >10% week-over-week traffic
price_sensitivity: If token price increases +10%: baseline margin impact ~ -2.7 ppts (assuming 60% reserved commit)
If token price decreases -10%: improved margin ~ +2.2 ppts and we can re-evaluate burst-to-reserve conversion to lock savings
Unit-econ tipping point: above 25% sustained token-price increase, consider re-negotiating model hosting tiers or accelerating quantization
Headcount elasticity: each additional 2 FTEs in optimization reduces effective token cost by ~0.6% (modeling A/B caching + batching enhancements)
stress_tests: Demand shock -25%: Reserve utilization falls <40%, runway extends by ~6 months but fixed reserved cost creates margin drag; action = aggressive redeploy/reassign infra and pause non-critical hires.
Demand shock +40%: On-demand spend grows 3.1x vs baseline; action = accelerate commit band increase to move to Band C within two billing cycles.
Price shock +50%: Immediate review with Procurement + Research; consider temporary price pass-through on enterprise committed tiers and short-term quota surcharge for self-serve.
estimated_impact: Move from Band A -> Band B (Q2->Q3): expected EBITDA delta +3.1 ppts after hiring and auto-scaling ops improvements.
Move from Band B -> Band C (Q3->Q4): additional EBITDA delta +2.0 ppts but increases downside risk if traffic drops >20%.
Switching 10% of traffic to on-device quantized variants reduces token spend by estimated 6% with one-time infra engineering cost of ~$350k.
